new_candidates.body:
### Is there an already existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

Related but different issues and PRs I found:

- #4901 (merged, 3.x only): "Fix Proxy block in TypeLookup Service". It is the closest precedent. The same PDP temporary proxy pool ran out there, but the slots were held by TypeLookup requests. That PR made TypeLookup copy the proxy. It did not touch the lock order described below.
- #6502: the event thread is blocked in `PDP::check_remote_participant_liveliness` there too. In that issue the PDP mutex holder waits in `ResourceEvent::unregister_timer`. In this one it waits in `ProxyPool::get()`.
- #3058 (closed as duplicate) and #5433 (closed): deadlocks when entities are created from inside listener callbacks, through `pairing_writer_proxy_with_any_local_reader` / `endpoints_list_mutex` and endpoint mutexes. Neither one involves the pool.
- #2717 added `ProxyPool`.

### Expected behavior

Application threads can call `Subscriber::create_datareader()` / `Publisher::create_datawriter()` (and delete them) concurrently, while other participants on the network create or delete endpoints, without the participant deadlocking.

### Current behavior

The participant deadlocks permanently. These threads are blocked:

- **One receive thread** (UDP or SHM) handling a remote SEDP subscription (or publication) announcement. It holds the **PDP mutex** and waits in `ProxyPool<WriterProxyData, 4>::get()`, on `cv_.wait` with no timeout, for a free temporary proxy.
- **Four application threads** inside `create_datareader()`. Each one holds one of the **4 pool slots** and waits for the **PDP mutex** in `PDP::lookupWriterProxyData()`.
- Bystanders end up blocked as well:
  - the event thread (`PDP::check_remote_participant_liveliness`)
  - the other receive threads (`PDP::assert_remote_participant_liveliness`)
  - threads deleting endpoints. These wait for `endpoints_list_mutex`, which the stuck receive thread holds shared through `forEachUserWriter`.

Discovery, liveliness and entity creation/deletion on that participant stop for good. The remote participants eventually drop it when its lease expires.

#### Root cause: ABBA between `PDP::mp_mutex` and `PDP::temp_writer_proxies_` (likewise `temp_reader_proxies_`)

`ProxyPool<Proxy, N = 4>` blocks in `get()` until a slot is free. `PDP::temp_reader_proxies_` and `PDP::temp_writer_proxies_` use the default `N = 4`, and it cannot be configured.

References are for v2.14.4 (346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89):

- [`include/fastrtps/utils/ProxyPool.hpp:105`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/include/fastrtps/utils/ProxyPool.hpp#L105) `template< class Proxy, std::size_t N = 4> class ProxyPool`
- [`include/fastrtps/utils/ProxyPool.hpp:217-237`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/include/fastrtps/utils/ProxyPool.hpp#L217-L237): `get()` waits on `cv_.wait(lock, [&]{ return mask_.any(); })` with no timeout.
- [`include/fastdds/rtps/builtin/discovery/participant/PDP.h:530-532`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/include/fastdds/rtps/builtin/discovery/participant/PDP.h#L530-L532) `ProxyPool<ReaderProxyData> temp_reader_proxies_; ProxyPool<WriterProxyData> temp_writer_proxies_;`

**Path A: local entity creation (application thread). Order: pool → PDP mutex**

```
Subscriber::create_datareader -> DataReaderImpl::enable -> RTPSParticipantImpl::registerReader
 -> BuiltinProtocols::addLocalReader -> EDP::newLocalReaderProxyData
 -> EDP::pairing_reader_proxy_with_any_local_writer          (called WITHOUT the PDP mutex)
    -> forEachUserWriter(lambda):
         auto temp = get_temporary_writer_proxies_pool().get();   // (1) takes a pool slot
         mp_PDP->lookupWriterProxyData(writerGUID, *temp);         // (2) locks PDP mutex
```

- [`EDP.cpp:249`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp#L249): `newLocalReaderProxyData` calls `pairing_reader_proxy_with_any_local_writer` without holding the PDP mutex.
- [`EDP.cpp:1151-1164`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp#L1151-L1164): the pool slot is taken at :1161 and `lookupWriterProxyData` is called at :1164.
- [`PDP.cpp:685-689`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/participant/PDP.cpp#L685-L689): `lookupWriterProxyData` takes `std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> guardPDP(*mp_mutex)`.

**Path B: remote SEDP announcement (receive thread). Order: PDP mutex → pool**

```
StatefulReader::change_received -> NotifyChanges
 -> EDPSimpleSUBListener::onNewCacheChangeAdded
    PREVENT_PDP_DEADLOCK(...)        // std::unique_lock on PDP mutex, held until return
    -> EDPBaseSUBListener::add_reader_from_change
       -> EDP::pairing_reader_proxy_with_any_local_writer
          -> forEachUserWriter(lambda):
               get_temporary_writer_proxies_pool().get();  // waits forever: all 4 slots
                                                           // are held by Path A threads
```

- [`EDPSimpleListeners.cpp:43-56`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDPSimpleListeners.cpp#L43-L56): `PREVENT_PDP_DEADLOCK` takes `std::unique_lock<std::recursive_mutex> lock(*((pdp)->getMutex()))` (line 47) for the rest of the caller's scope.
- [`EDPSimpleListeners.cpp:263-266`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDPSimpleListeners.cpp#L263-L266): `PREVENT_PDP_DEADLOCK` is followed by `add_reader_from_change`.
- [`EDPSimpleListeners.cpp:229`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDPSimpleListeners.cpp#L229) calls `edp->pairing_reader_proxy_with_any_local_writer(...)`, which reaches the pool `get()` at `EDP.cpp:1161`.

When four Path A threads each take a slot and then block on the PDP mutex, Path B holds that mutex while waiting for a slot. Nothing can make progress after that.

The same cycle exists on the writer side with the reader pool:
- `EDP::newLocalWriterProxyData` ([`EDP.cpp:392`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp#L392)) calls `pairing_writer_proxy_with_any_local_reader` ([`EDP.cpp:1358-1371`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp#L1358-L1371)), which does pool `get()` then `lookupReaderProxyData`.
- On the remote side, `EDPSimplePUBListener::onNewCacheChangeAdded` ([`EDPSimpleListeners.cpp:149-152`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDPSimpleListeners.cpp#L149-L152)) calls `add_writer_from_change`, which calls `pairing_writer_proxy_with_any_local_reader` (:117).

Both sides reproduce with the program below. The security-only variants (`pairing_reader_proxy_with_local_writer` / `pairing_writer_proxy_with_local_reader`) use the same pattern.

Note that `EDP::pairingReader` / `EDP::pairingWriter` already lock the PDP mutex first ([`EDP.cpp:972`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp#L972), [`:1064`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp#L1064)). The comment on `PREVENT_PDP_DEADLOCK` says "PDP mutex should always be first". `pairing_*_with_any_local_*` breaks that rule only when it is reached from the local-entity path.

#### Affected versions

- **Reproduced:** v2.14.4. I have not run the reproducer on any other version.
- **Reproduced on `master`** (980f1926, 2026-10-14) with the regression test of #6576, which is a port of the reproducer below to the 3.x API. The stacks have the same shape; on 3.x the local entry points are `EDP::new_reader_proxy_data` / `new_writer_proxy_data`, and the listener reaches `pairing_*_with_any_local_*` through the `TypeLookupManager::async_get_type` callback in `add_*_from_change`.
- **Unchanged by source inspection:** v2.14.5, v2.14.6, v2.14.7 (010b908d), the `2.14.x` head (5fb2d46b, 2026-10-14) and `master` (980f1926). These have the same pool size, the same `get()`, the same unlocked call from `new_reader_proxy_data` / `newLocalReaderProxyData`, and the same `PREVENT_PDP_DEADLOCK` → `add_*_from_change` → `pairing_*_with_any_local_*` path. On master see [`src/cpp/utils/ProxyPool.hpp:105`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/67778b925fe6ed15711d79fb12029bcc2f5afa00/src/cpp/utils/ProxyPool.hpp#L105), [`EDP.cpp:1304-1317`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/67778b925fe6ed15711d79fb12029bcc2f5afa00/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp#L1304-L1317) and [`EDPSimpleListeners.cpp:330-333`](https://github.com/eProsima/Fast-DDS/blob/67778b925fe6ed15711d79fb12029bcc2f5afa00/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDPSimpleListeners.cpp#L330-L333).
- **Older releases:** the pool came in with #2717 (2022) and is also in v2.6.10, so releases since then are likely affected too.

### Steps to reproduce

Self-contained reproducer (public DDS API only, ~400 lines, plus a Dockerfile that builds Fast DDS v2.14.4 from source on `ubuntu:22.04`): **https://gist.github.com/SeanChangX/ac9a7e8c5c4cf02fb187baaab8b4c75b**

Two processes run on the same host:

1. **"local"**:
   - one participant with 32 long-lived DataWriters, so every `create_datareader()` iterates `forEachUserWriter`
   - 8 threads, each on its own topic, looping `create_datareader()` / `delete_datareader()`
2. **"peer"**: a second participant with 4 threads looping `create_datareader()` / `delete_datareader()`, which produces a constant stream of remote SEDP subscription announcements.

A watchdog in "local" reports a deadlock when no create/delete completes for 10 s. It then attaches gdb and dumps all thread stacks.

```
docker build -t fastdds-proxypool-deadlock .
docker run --rm --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE fastdds-proxypool-deadlock            # reader side
docker run --rm --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE fastdds-proxypool-deadlock \
       /opt/repro/run_repro.sh --side writer                               # writer side
```

Results on v2.14.4, x86_64, container limited to 4 CPUs, 120 s per run:

| local threads | local long-lived endpoints | side   | runs | deadlocked | time to deadlock |
|---------------|----------------------------|--------|------|------------|------------------|
| 8             | 32 writers                 | reader | 5    | 5          | ≤ 0.5 s          |
| 8             | 32 readers                 | writer | 2    | 2          | ≤ 0.5 s          |
| 4             | 32 writers                 | reader | 2    | 2          | 0.5 s, 1.5 s     |
| 4             | 4 writers                  | reader | 1    | 1          | 2 s              |
| 8             | 1 writer                   | reader | 1    | 1          | 3 s              |
| 4             | 1 writer                   | reader | 2    | 0          | (no deadlock in 120 s, ~1.9 M cycles each) |
| **3**         | 32 writers                 | reader | 1    | **0**      | (no deadlock in 120 s, ~0.5 M cycles) |
| 16            | **0** writers              | reader | 1    | **0**      | (no deadlock in 120 s, ~1.9 M cycles) |

The controls match the analysis:
- With 3 creator threads the pool can never be fully held by Path A threads, so there is no deadlock.
- With no local writers `forEachUserWriter` never touches the pool, so there is no deadlock.
- With exactly 4 threads and 1 writer the window is narrow, and it did not trigger in 2 × 120 s.

Every deadlock had the same signature: one receive thread in `ProxyPool<…>::get()` and four creator threads in `PDP::lookupWriterProxyData` (reader side) or `PDP::lookupReaderProxyData` (writer side).

The production case matches this: an application creates many DataReaders and clients from several threads in parallel (for example at start-up, or when it brings a subsystem up again) while other participants on the same host join and leave. It hangs at start-up, only rarely, but it never recovers.

### Fast DDS version/commit

v2.14.4 (346159b5c3753221abdda0663b9c1253e16a7c89), with Fast CDR v2.2.5 and foonathan_memory_vendor v1.3.1. The code path is unchanged up to v2.14.7 and master (see above).

### Platform/Architecture

Other. Please specify in Additional context section.
- Production: Linux aarch64, Ubuntu 22.04 (Jammy).
- Reproducer: Ubuntu Jammy 22.04 amd64 (Docker container).

### Transport layer

Default configuration (UDPv4 + SHM, builtin transports). The receive thread that holds the PDP mutex has been seen to be the UDP receive thread and also the SHM one.

### Additional context

#### Observed stacks (from the reproducer; production stacks have the same shape)

Receive thread. It holds the PDP mutex (taken by `PREVENT_PDP_DEADLOCK` in frame 8) and waits for a pool slot:
```
#1  pthread_cond_wait
#2  std::condition_variable::wait<...ProxyPool<WriterProxyData,4>::get()::lambda>
#3  eprosima::ProxyPool<WriterProxyData, 4ul>::get           include/fastrtps/utils/ProxyPool.hpp:222
#4  operator()                                               rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp:1161
#5  RTPSParticipantImpl::forEachUserWriter<...>              rtps/participant/RTPSParticipantImpl.h:1011
#6  EDP::pairing_reader_proxy_with_any_local_writer          rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp:1159
#7  EDPBaseSUBListener::add_reader_from_change               rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDPSimpleListeners.cpp:229
#8  EDPSimpleSUBListener::onNewCacheChangeAdded              rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDPSimpleListeners.cpp:266
#9  StatefulReader::NotifyChanges                            rtps/reader/StatefulReader.cpp:1253
#10 StatefulReader::change_received                          rtps/reader/StatefulReader.cpp:1172
#11 StatefulReader::processDataMsg                           rtps/reader/StatefulReader.cpp:660
    ... MessageReceiver::processCDRMsg -> ReceiverResource::OnDataReceived
#19 UDPChannelResource::perform_listen_operation             (thread "dds.udp.<port>")
```

Four application threads, identical stacks. Each holds a pool slot (frame 7, `EDP.cpp:1161`) and waits for the PDP mutex:
```
#1  pthread_mutex_lock
#4  std::recursive_mutex::lock
#6  PDP::lookupWriterProxyData                               rtps/builtin/discovery/participant/PDP.cpp:689
#7  operator()                                               rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp:1164
#8  RTPSParticipantImpl::forEachUserWriter<...>              rtps/participant/RTPSParticipantImpl.h:1011
#9  EDP::pairing_reader_proxy_with_any_local_writer          rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp:1159
#10 EDP::newLocalReaderProxyData                             rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp:249
#11 BuiltinProtocols::addLocalReader                         rtps/builtin/BuiltinProtocols.cpp:242
#12 RTPSParticipantImpl::registerReader                      rtps/participant/RTPSParticipantImpl.cpp:1645
#14 DataReaderImpl::enable                                   fastdds/subscriber/DataReaderImpl.cpp:299
#18 SubscriberImpl::create_datareader                        fastdds/subscriber/SubscriberImpl.cpp:238
#19 Subscriber::create_datareader                            fastdds/subscriber/Subscriber.cpp:112
```

Bystanders:
```
"dds.ev.0":        PDP::check_remote_participant_liveliness     -> blocked on PDP mutex
"dds.udp.7400":    PDP::assert_remote_participant_liveliness    -> blocked on PDP mutex   (other receive threads, UDP and SHM)
app threads:       Subscriber::delete_datareader -> RTPSParticipantImpl::deleteUserEndpoint
                   -> blocked on endpoints_list_mutex (held shared by the stuck receive thread
                      via forEachUserWriter) or on the PDP mutex (PDP::removeReaderProxyData)
```

#### Suggested fix

Any one of these breaks the cycle. They are listed from smallest change to most robust.

1. **Take the PDP mutex before the pool in `pairing_*_with_any_local_*`.** This is the same order `pairingReader` / `pairingWriter` and the EDP listeners already use. The PDP mutex is recursive, so the listener path, which already holds it, does not change. The local path becomes PDP → endpoints list (shared) → pool, the same order as the listener path. The patch below on v2.14.4 removes the deadlock in the reproducer (results below).

   ```diff
   --- a/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp
   +++ b/src/cpp/rtps/builtin/discovery/endpoint/EDP.cpp
   @@ bool EDP::pairing_reader_proxy_with_any_local_writer(
        EPROSIMA_LOG_INFO(RTPS_EDP, rdata->guid() << " in topic: \"" << rdata->topicName() << "\"");
    
   +    // The PDP mutex must be taken before a temporary proxy is taken from the pool, as done by
   +    // the EDP listeners. Otherwise threads holding pool slots while waiting for the PDP mutex
   +    // can starve a thread that holds the PDP mutex while waiting for a pool slot.
   +    std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> pdp_guard(*mp_PDP->getMutex());
   +
        mp_RTPSParticipant->forEachUserWriter([&, rdata](RTPSWriter& w) -> bool
   @@ bool EDP::pairing_writer_proxy_with_any_local_reader(
        EPROSIMA_LOG_INFO(RTPS_EDP, wdata->guid() << " in topic: \"" << wdata->topicName() << "\"");
    
   +    // See pairing_reader_proxy_with_any_local_writer: PDP mutex before the temporary proxy pool.
   +    std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> pdp_guard(*mp_PDP->getMutex());
   +
        mp_RTPSParticipant->forEachUserReader([&, wdata](RTPSReader& r) -> bool
   ```

   A narrower version takes the lock inside the lambda, before `get()`, and releases it after `temp_*_proxy_data.reset()`. That avoids holding PDP across `matched_*_add`, but the listener path already holds PDP there.

2. **Avoid the pool for these lookups.** For example:
   - have `PDP::lookupWriterProxyData` / `lookupReaderProxyData` take a callback that runs `valid_matching` on the stored proxy under the PDP mutex, so no copy is needed; or
   - copy into a stack or thread-local proxy, as #4901 did for TypeLookup.

3. **Make `ProxyPool::get()` non-blocking.** When the pool is empty it could fall back to a heap-allocated proxy instead of waiting. Any other thread that waits on the pool while holding a lock would then not deadlock.

4. **Mitigation only:** make the pool size configurable or larger. This only raises the number of concurrent creator threads needed to trigger the deadlock.

I applied fix 1 to v2.14.4 and ran the reproducer again with the same settings. It ran 6 times for 120 s each:
- 3 runs on the reader side with 8 threads and 32 writers
- 2 runs on the writer side with 8 threads and 32 readers
- 1 run on the reader side with 16 threads and 32 writers

None of the runs deadlocked. Each one completed about 1.26 to 1.48 M create/delete cycles. Unpatched, every one of these configurations deadlocked within 0.5 s.

#6576 applies this change to `master` and adds a blackbox regression test (`DDSDiscovery.concurrent_local_{reader,writer}_creation_while_discovering_remote_{readers,writers}_does_not_deadlock`). Without the fix the test hung in every run; with it, it passed 20 out of 20 repetitions.

#### Workaround

Serialize entity creation/deletion inside the application, so that at most 3 threads are in `create_datareader` / `create_datawriter` at once per participant. Lazy creation from many worker threads at once (for example clients or readers created on first use) is what triggers this.

If the application does not need endpoints of the same participant to match each other, setting the participant property `fastdds.ignore_local_endpoints` to `true` also avoids it, because `pairing_*_with_any_local_*` is then not called from the local path.

### XML configuration file

None (default QoS, builtin transports).

### Relevant log output

No Fast DDS log output. The process simply stops making progress. Reproducer output:

```
[peer] pid=7 domain=0 side=reader threads=4 fixed=0 topics=8 stall=30s
[local] pid=8 domain=0 side=reader threads=8 fixed=32 topics=8 stall=10s
[watchdog] DEADLOCK: no create/delete progress for 10 s; stalled at t=10.5s (first stalled ~0.5s after start) after 89 cycles
<gdb thread apply all bt>
RESULT: deadlock reproduced
```

### Network traffic capture

Not applicable. The reproducer runs both participants on one host. Only the timing of SEDP announcements matters, not their content.
new_candidates.title: Deadlock between PDP mutex and the temporary proxy pool (`ProxyPool<..., 4>`) when ≥ 4 threads create DataReaders/DataWriters concurrently while remote endpoints are discovered
